feedback: Iteration 0 gave the following evidence. Off-track ended 59 of 60 runs with max_error about 0.065 m, just over the 0.06 m limit, while rms_error stayed at 0.016 to 0.022 m. Failures are transient excursions, not steady drift. Line-loss events were 1.35 to 1.9 per run, highest on the slalom. Oval finish time was 1.73 s, so the drivetrain is not limiting. Based on this, the Integrator's next controller will need to rescale gains to a wider span and will keep base_speed at 1.5. Before the next race I cannot state how this design will perform. Decide from the next race as follows. If line_loss_events fall below about 1 and max_error stays under 0.06 m, keep the span and change only the lead: try y = 0.04 if oscillation rises. If line losses remain above about 1 on the slalom, widen the span further. If the robot finishes the oval but still ends off-track on the s-bend or slalom, the limit is turn speed, not sensing, so lower mass or widen wheel_track.
requested_changes: If line_loss_events stay above about 1 on the s-bend or slalom, try sensor_positions at x = -0.04, -0.02, 0, 0.02, 0.04 with sensor_size 0.016 (span 80 mm, pitch 20 mm). Iteration 0 showed 1.9 line losses on the slalom with a 40 mm span, so a wider span is the next lever. Scale kp up about 1.3 to keep the steering gain.
If steering_oscillation rises above about 0.3 while line losses fall, move all sensors to y = 0.04 at the current span. This adds lead to counter the jitter that the shorter y = 0.03 lead may cause.

If completion stays at 0 on the oval and s-bend while max_error is under 0.06 m, try wheel_track 0.10 and mass 0.6. Iteration 0 showed the oval finishing in 1.73 s, so this is a fallback only, to test whether turn rate is the limit.
